proposed_quote: NH2-terminal amino acid sequence analysis of purified extracellular hemolysin (HpmA) confirmed the cleavage of the 29-amino-acid leader peptide in the secreted form of HpmA. Hemolysis assays and immunoblot analysis ... indicated that HpmB is necessary for the extracellular secretion and activation of HpmA.
notes: Ref 10.1128/jb.172.3.1206-1216.1990 (Uphoff & Welch 1990, J Bacteriol, PMC208585) resolves and IS about P. mirabilis HpmA, documents secretion (HpmB-dependent extracellular secretion of HpmA). BUT the citation_quote names FhaC mediating HpmA secretion, which is NOT in this paper (FhaC is the Bordetella TpsB; that statement comes from a cross-complementation study). Quote not found in abstract or full-text. Proposed verbatim secretion sentence from same ref's abstract.

Ref 10.1107/S174430911302962X (Baelen et al. 2013, Acta Cryst F, PMC3855712) resolves, H. influenzae HxuA. Quote verbatim in abstract: "HxuA is secreted by its specific transporter HxuB. HxuA/HxuB belongs to the so-called two-partner secretion systems (TPSs)...". Documents TPS (T5bSS) secretion.

Ref 10.1128/IAI.72.4.1874-1884.2004 (Ward, Mock, Hansen 2004, Infect Immun, PMC375143) resolves, H. ducreyi 35000. Quote verbatim in PMC abstract/full text: "The LspA1 and LspA2 proteins of [Haemophilus ducreyi] 35000 are two very large macromolecules that can be detected in concentrated culture supernatant fluid." (Europe PMC strips organism string; PubMed full text confirms). Documents secretion: supernatant detection + LspB-dependent release.

Same ref as T5SS_13 (10.1128/IAI.72.4.1874-1884.2004, PMC375143). Quote covers both LspA1 and LspA2 verbatim. lspB/lspA2 mutants did not release detectable LspA2; supernatant detection documents T5bSS secretion. H. ducreyi 35000 matches.

Ref 10.1016/j.ijmm.2013.11.021 (Pramanik, Konninger, Selvam, Braun 2014, IJMM, PMID 24462008) resolves, S. marcescens ShlA/ShlB. Quote verbatim in abstract: "The ShlA hemolysin of Serratia marcescens is secreted across the outer membrane by the ShlB protein; ShlB belongs to the two-partner secretion system (type Vb)". Documents T5bSS secretion. Paper does not name Db11 strain but ShlA/ShlB is the canonical conserved S. marcescens TPS hemolysin; same species, organism_match=yes.

Ref 10.1084/jem.20020407 (Comanducci et al. 2002, J Exp Med, PMC2193550) resolves, N. meningitidis MC58, correct organism. Quote IS verbatim in abstract. BUT under STRICT rubric it documents ADHESIN structure + epithelial binding ("similar to a novel class of adhesins... binds to epithelial cells"), NOT secretion. Full text shows surface exposure (OMV western, FACS) of an OM-anchored adhesin but no autotransporter secretion/export assay; this is a vaccine-antigen paper predating TAA/T5cSS export characterization. No secretion sentence available in this ref. Flag for human review; do not auto-replace.

Ref 10.1093/emboj/19.22.5989 (Hoiczyk et al. 2000, EMBO J, PMC305836) resolves. Quote verbatim in abstract: "an N-terminal oval head domain is followed by a putative coiled-coil rod and terminated by a C-terminal membrane anchor domain." BUT this is a STRUCTURE/domain-architecture paper on YadA/UspA adhesins; documents adhesin structure and surface projections, NOT secretion/export (no supernatant, translocation, or machinery-dependent export assay). Organism: paper covers YadA of enteropathogenic Yersinia generically; row is Y. enterocolitica 8081 (strain_diff). weak: no experimental secretion evidence in this ref.

Ref 10.1111/j.1462-2920.2010.02174.x (Salacha et al. 2010, Environ Microbiol, PMID 20192961) resolves, P. aeruginosa PAO1. Both quote spans verbatim in abstract/full text: "We discovered a novel secreted protein by Pseudomonas aeruginosa, PlpD" and "The association between a TpsB component and a passenger protein is a unique hybrid organization that we propose to classify as Type Vd." (ellipsis joins them). Documents secretion (T5dSS archetype). No PMCID; verified via Europe PMC + web.

Ref 10.1371/journal.pone.0047069 (Oberhettinger et al. 2012, PLoS One, PMC3467248). Both quote spans verbatim in abstract: "the N-terminal beta-barrel domain acts as a translocation pore to secrete the C-terminal passenger domain" and "propose that this class of autotransporters be termed Type Ve secretion." Documents autotransporter (T5eSS) secretion; biogenesis Bam/SurA-dependent. Paper covers intimin/invasin of enteropathogenic Yersinia/E. coli; row is E. coli O157:H7 Sakai eae, conserved T5eSS effector family, strain_diff acceptable.
